q: To whom did Paul address this letter?
a: Paul addressed this letter to all the people who are set apart in Christ Jesus at Philippi, including the overseers and deacons.

q: For what did Paul give thanks to God for the Philippians?
a: Paul gave thanks to God for the Philippians’ fellowship in the gospel from the first day until now.

q: Of what was Paul confident regarding the Philippians?
a: Paul was confident that he who had begun a good work in them would complete it.

q: In what had the Philippians been Paul’s partners?
a: In Paul’s imprisonment, and in his defense and confirmation of the gospel, the Philippians had been his partners.

q: What did Paul pray would increase more and more among the Philippians?
a: Paul prayed that love would increase more and more among the Philippians.

q: With what did Paul desire that the Philippians be filled?
a: Paul desired that the Philippians be filled with the fruits of righteousness.

q: How had Paul’s imprisonment advanced the gospel?
a: Paul’s imprisonment for Christ had become widely known, and most of the brothers were now speaking with more boldness.

q: Why were some proclaiming Christ out of selfish and insincere motives?
a: Some were proclaiming Christ out of selfish and insincere motives thinking they were adding to Paul’s affliction in prison.

q: What was Paul’s reaction to the sincere and insincere preaching of Christ?
a: Paul rejoiced that, either way, Christ was being proclaimed.

q: What did Paul desire to do in life or by death?
a: Paul desired to bring glory to Christ either in life or by death.

q: Paul said that to live is what, and to die is what?
a: Paul said that to live is Christ, and to die is gain.

q: What choices pulled Paul in different directions?
a: Paul was pulled by the choices of being with Christ in death or of remaining in the flesh to continue his labor.

q: For what purpose was Paul confident that he would remain with the Philippians?
a: Paul was confident that he would remain with the Philippians for their progress and joy in the faith.

q: Whether with the Philippians or away from them, what did Paul want to hear about the Philippians?
a: Paul wanted to hear that the Philippians stood fast in one spirit, with one soul striving together for the faith of the gospel.

q: When the Philippians did not fear those opposing them, of what was that a sign?
a: When the Philippians did not fear those opposing them, it was a sign of their opponents’ destruction, but of the believers’ salvation.

q: What two things had been granted to the Philippians by God?
a: It had been granted to the Philippians that they believe on Christ, but also that they suffer on his behalf.

q: What does Paul say the Philippians must do to make his joy full?
a: The Philippians must be of the same mind, have the same love, and be united in spirit and mind.

q: How does Paul say the Philippians should consider each other?
a: The Philippians should consider each other better than themselves.

q: Whose mind does Paul say we need to have?
a: Paul says we need to have the mind of Christ Jesus.

q: In what form did Christ Jesus exist?
a: Christ Jesus existed in the form of God.

q: What form did Christ Jesus then take?
a: Christ Jesus then took the form of a servant, in the appearance of a man.

q: How did Jesus humble himself?
a: Jesus humbled himself by obeying to the point of death on the cross.

q: What did God then do for Jesus?
a: God highly exalted Jesus and gave him the name above every name.

q: What will every tongue confess?
a: Every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord.

q: How are the Philippians called to work out their salvation?
a: The Philippians are to work out their salvation with fear and trembling.

q: What does God work in believers to do?
a: God works in believers both to will and to work for his good pleasure.

q: Everything must be done without what?
a: Everything must be done without complaining and arguing.

q: For what purpose is Paul pouring out his life?
a: Paul is pouring out his life in the sacrifice and service of the Philippian’s faith.

q: Why is Timothy a unique helper for Paul?
a: Timothy is unique because he truly cares for the Philippians.

q: Is Paul expecting to see the Philippians?
a: Yes, Paul expects to see the Philippians soon.

q: For what did Epaphroditus almost die?
a: Epaphroditus almost died doing the work of Christ, serving Paul and supplying Paul’s needs.

q: For whom does Paul warn the believers to watch out?
a: Paul warns the believers to watch out for the dogs, the evil workers, and the mutilators.

q: Who does Paul say are the true circumcision?
a: Paul says the true circumcision are those who worship in the Spirit of God, glory in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh.

q: How does Paul describe his previous conduct in respect to the righteousness of the law?
a: Paul describes his previous conduct as blameless in respect to the righteousness of the law.

q: How does Paul now regard his previous confidence in the flesh?
a: Paul now counts all his previous confidence in the flesh as worthless because of Christ.

q: For what purpose does Paul now consider all the previous things as garbage?
a: Paul considers all the previous things as garbage so that he may gain Christ.

q: What righteousness does Paul now have?
a: Paul now has the righteousness from God that is through faith in Christ.

q: Paul has fellowship with Christ in what?
a: Paul has the fellowship of Christ’s sufferings.

q: Although he is not yet complete, what does Paul continue to do?
a: Paul pursues perfection to grasp the reason for which Jesus grasped him.

q: Toward what goal does Paul press on?
a: Paul presses on toward the goal to win the prize of the upward calling of God in Christ Jesus.

q: What does Paul tell the Philippians to do regarding the example of his walk?
a: Paul tells the Philippians to join and imitate him in his walk.

q: What is the destiny of those whose god is their belly and who think about earthly things?
a: Those whose god is their belly and who think about earthly things are destined for destruction.

q: Where does Paul say the citizenship of believers is located?
a: Paul says the citizenship of believers is in heaven.

q: What will Christ do to the bodies of believers when he comes from heaven?
a: Christ will transform the lowly bodies of believers into bodies formed like his glorious body.

q: What does Paul want his beloved friends in Philippi to do?
a: Paul wants the Philippians to stand firm in the Lord.

q: What does Paul wish to see happen with Euodia and Syntyche?
a: Paul wishes to see Euodia and Syntyche have the same mind in the Lord.

q: What does Paul tell the Philippians to always do?
a: Paul tells them to rejoice in the Lord always.

q: Instead of being anxious, what does Paul say to do?
a: Paul says that instead of being anxious, we are to tell God in prayer what we need, and thank him.

q: If we do this, what will guard our hearts and thoughts?
a: If we do this, the peace of God will guard our hearts and thoughts.

q: Upon what kinds of things does Paul say to think?
a: Paul says to think upon things that are honorable, just, pure, lovely, of good report, excellent, and praiseworthy.

q: What have the Philippians now been able to renew?
a: The Philippians have now been able to renew their concern for Paul.

q: What secret has Paul learned about living in different circumstances?
a: Paul has learned the secret of living contently in both abundance and need.

q: By what power can Paul live contently?
a: Paul can live contently in all circumstances through Christ, who strengthens him.

q: What does Paul seek for the Philippians in their giving to provide for his needs?
a: Paul seeks the fruit that increases to the Philippians’ account.

q: How does God view the gift made by the Philippians to Paul?
a: God is pleased with the gift that the Philippians have made to Paul.

q: What does Paul say God will do for the Philippians?
a: Paul says that God will supply every need of the Philippians according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.

q: Paul says that those of which household greet the Philippians?
a: Those of Caesar’s household greet the Philippians.
